title: Grateful Dead Live at Frost Amphitheatre - Stanford University on 1982-10-10

ai_review.summary: An outstanding audience recording with crystal‑clear guitar and bass that captures a high‑energy show highlighted by a scorching Crazy Fingers and an emotional Lost Sailor/Saint of Circumstance.
ai_review.review: The crowd‑tape is praised as one of the best ever on the Archive – the mics placed near the monitors deliver astonishing clarity, making the guitars, bass and even the drum ambience feel like you’re front‑row. Musically the concert shines with a blazing Crazy Fingers, superb China>Rider, a transcendent Lost Sailor/Saint, plus memorable moments from Red Rooster, Playing in the Band and more, all delivered with high energy throughout.

ai_rating.rationale: All 14 reviews are overwhelmingly positive (12 × 5‑star, 2 × 4‑star). Both the performance and the audio quality are described as exceptional, justifying a rating near the top of the scale.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mics positioned on the monitors give a crisp, “soundboard‑like” clarity; guitar tone is stunning, bass response during drums is described as insane, and overall the tape sounds like you’re right in front of the band with minimal noise.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows smoothly from a mellow, high‑energy opening into tighter jams; highlights like China>Rider segue nicely into Crazy Fingers and the emotive Lost Sailor/Saint, keeping momentum high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's guitar tone is repeatedly called stunning; notable slide solo on Red Rooster and a crisp midi‑guitar passage are highlighted.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass response is described as insane, especially during the drum segment, indicating powerful low‑end work.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob’s vocals and his improvisational “rain” spoken words in Looks Like Rain are praised; his onstage banter (vote‑yes comment) adds to the show’s vibe.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drums provide a solid, driving foundation with a bass response that feels immersive.
